scope: Standing connected 1899–1921 Tamozawa Imperial Villa including its copper roofs, the raised central three-story residence and open courtyards, in Nikkō.

primaryWrittenSources.facts: The prefectural record describes the surviving connected villa as a timber structure mostly one story high with two- and three-story parts, copper shingle roofs, approximately 4500 square metres of floor space and present form established by 1921.
The memorial park identifies the three-story Edo-era Tokugawa residence moved to the site and incorporated into the extended imperial villa, with 106 rooms and retained garden.
